clue.text: Summary investigation of personal bag

parts.note: a summary is a brief, a short statement of the facts
a case is a matter under investigation, as by police

explanation.surface: A quick inquiry into someone's private luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefcase is a flat case for carrying papers, a bag for one's own business use.

clue.text: Abrupt dismissal of genteel writing in a fleeting encounter

indicators.note: in means these pieces are set inside the next word

parts.note: a brush is a brief encounter, as a brush with the law
U means upper-class, socially acceptable
MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Being thrown out over some posh handwriting during a brief meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The bum's rush is forcible ejection, as of an unwanted guest.

clue.text: Entrance to a small bay

definitions.meaning: a way in, as an opening for water
a narrow arm of the sea or a lake running inland

explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is both an opening that lets something in and a small coastal creek.

clue.text: "Firebird" found out of place with Tchaikovsky's First — we can't have this!

indicators.note: out of place means the letters are put in different places

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: First means the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A ballet title misplaced alongside a Tchaikovsky first symphony, which is not allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Firebird is a ballet by Stravinsky, not Tchaikovsky, so it is out of place; T, the first letter of Tchaikovsky's, joins FIREBIRD and FOUND in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbidden fruit is anything desired but not allowed, from the apple of Eden.

clue.text: Refrain that keeps flyers up to the mark

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the piece is read from bottom to top

parts.note: BA is British Airways, an airline of flyers
a stain is a mark

explanation.surface: A song's chorus about pilots keeping up to standard.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain, to hold back from doing something.

clue.text: In rivalry, note Greek character, poor soul

parts.note: E is a musical note
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Competing, a poor soul writes down a note and a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulous means eager to emulate, competing with others.

clue.text: Big about turning up for work!

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for big sizes

indicators.note: turning means the word beside it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a large piece of work that has shown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big' as OS (outsize) is a clothing-label convention; 'turning' acts only on 'up', and 'about' puts OS round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for a work, used of a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: To produce an ingredient for dye is the plan hothead and I devised

indicators.note: devised means worked out, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the head, or first letter, of hot is H

explanation.surface: A hothead and I hatched a scheme to make dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Phthaleins are chemical compounds used to make dyes.

clue.text: In place of your original regular?

parts.note: in stead of means in place of

indicators.note: original means the first letter of the word, its origin

explanation.surface: Asking whether a substitute can take over your customer's place.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend.

clue.text: Archie with Rosie, arrested during prize hold-up, getting it overturned on a dropped charge

indicators.note: arrested during means these pieces are held inside the other one
hold-up in a down clue means the piece is lifted to read bottom to top

parts.note: a cup is a prize
Archie Rice is the music-hall comedian in John Osborne's play The Entertainer
rosie is treated as rosy, a shade of red

indicators.note: overturned means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people are nabbed during a robbery, then the verdict is reversed and the charge dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'hold-up' turns the prize to read PUC; 'arrested during' holds the two names inside it. 'charge' looks criminal but means a price.
explanation.definitionFit: A price reduction drops what is charged, punning on a criminal charge dropped.

clue.text: Tooth doctor a household god?

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
a lar is one of the Lares, the Roman household gods

explanation.surface: A question whether a dentist might be worshipped at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A molar is a back grinding tooth.

clue.text: Pert songstress with fractured toe Buster stands in for

indicators.note: fractured means broken, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An understudy named Buster steps in for a singer whose toe is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A soubrette is a stock comic role in opera or theatre: a flirtatious, saucy young maid who sings.

clue.text: Wine delivered in topless metal box, which is to be returned

indicators.note: to be returned means the trimmed word is sent back, read from end to start
topless means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a canister is a metal box for tea or similar

explanation.surface: Wine arrives in a lidless tin that must be sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes C off CANISTER to leave ANISTER, which 'to be returned' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Fruit producer's goldfish died

parts.note: split as gold (or, heraldic gold) and fish (char, a fish of the trout family)
d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A gardener's goldfish has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goldfish' is read as two words, gold and fish, each giving letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plantation of fruit trees, so it produces fruit.

clue.text: Look around! Hang spring upheaval of getting rid of the money

indicators.note: around means the first word is placed round the rest

parts.note: see means look
pend means hang, as in pendant and pending

indicators.note: an upheaval is a violent disturbance, so the letters of the word before it are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A frantic exhortation about a messy spring clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look around!' reads as a command, but the word for look is the container; 'upheaval' rearranges the letters of spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A spending spree is a bout of lavish buying, a way of getting rid of cash fast.

clue.text: Recurrent rap pedestrian gets caught in

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A walker is caught up in repeated rapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrapped means trapped, caught by a trick or snare.

clue.text: Yes man finds three quarters to be in flower

indicators.note: to be in means the piece is placed inside the next word

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower
S, E and N are three of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A sycophant reckons three quarters of something will bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three quarters' looks like a fraction to take, but it means three compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: An assenter is one who agrees, a yes man.

clue.text: Packed comestibles, the produce of Indian forests?

indicators.note: what is produced from these letters is a new arrangement of them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A whimsical question whether canned food grows in the jungles of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardines in a tin are packed tightly, so the tin is a can of packed food.

clue.text: Poet, a little bit of a thing, meeting the Queen

parts.words: a little bit of a thing
parts.note: a fleck is a tiny speck or particle
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A minor poet has an audience with the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: James Elroy Flecker was an English poet, author of Hassan.

clue.text: Watery, unthatched abode agents come up about

indicators.note: about means the reversed piece goes round the next
come up in a down clue means the piece reads bottom to top

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency, its agents

indicators.note: unthatched means the top, the first letter, is taken off

parts.note: a squat is an occupied dwelling, an abode

explanation.surface: Spies rise up around a soggy roofless hut.
explanation.walkthrough: A squat is an illegally occupied house; 'unthatched' leaves QUAT and 'come up' gives AIC, which goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquatic means living in or relating to water.

clue.text: Left-winger supports resort being saved

indicators.note: supports in a down clue means this piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
a red is a left-winger, a communist

explanation.surface: A socialist props up a holiday town that has been rescued.
explanation.definitionFit: Spared means saved, let off from harm.

clue.text: Couple have right to seperate, that's plain

indicators.note: to separate means the letter splits the word around it (the clue misspells separate)

parts.note: a pair is a couple
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A couple who have the right to split up, and that's clear.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside PAIR after its P, giving PRAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide grassy plain of North America.

clue.text: Open denial about small measure in employment

indicators.note: in means the piece goes inside the next one

parts.note: use means employment, as in putting to use

indicators.note: about means the word goes round the next piece

parts.note: no is a denial
cl is a centilitre, a small measure

explanation.surface: A frank refusal over a small matter at work.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclose is an old word for to open, the reverse of to shut.

clue.text: Fruit starters for office lunch in vegetarian eatery

indicators.note: starters means the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A vegetarian restaurant serves this fruit for workers' lunches.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is a small stone fruit.

clue.text: Dad, to irritate, gets into row about mending equipment

indicators.note: gets into means these pieces go inside the word that follows
about means the word for row is turned round

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
pa is a familiar word for dad
irk means to irritate

explanation.surface: A father gets annoyed in a quarrel over fixing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives REIT from the word for row, and 'gets into' splits it after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A repair kit is a set of tools and patches for fixing things.

clue.text: One did almost nothing with time, being a fool

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone who idled away the hours is called a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a fool, a stupid person.

clue.text: Double celebrations are a thing of the past

indicators.note: double means the piece is written twice

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Holding two parties at once is no longer done.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo is extinct, so it stands for anything obsolete, as in dead as a dodo.

clue.text: Rector distracted by aunt, interminable storyteller

indicators.note: distracted means confused, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: interminable means without end, so the last letter of aunt goes

explanation.surface: A clergyman is driven to distraction by an aunt who goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminable' cuts AUNT to AUN, which joins RECTOR to make the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is someone who tells stories skilfully.
